nodes.title: Integral Hodge data
nodes.statement: Fix p>2, a Hodge-type datum (G,X), v|p of E(G,X), and a symplectic embedding with a Z_(p)-lattice Λ. Integral Hodge data consist of a point of the extended building, its full fixer G^fix and connected parahoric G°, a closed lattice realization of the required model, a finite tensor family cutting out that model, and compatible sufficiently small prime-to-p Siegel levels. Record whether the embedding is good or very good; neither adjective is implicit. For neat compatible K^p and K_p=G^fix(Z_p), define S as the normalization of the Zariski closure of Sh_K(G,X) in the chosen integral Siegel model after base change to O_(E,v), or to its completion O_E. Its generic fibre is Sh_K(G,X). The construction retains the actual induced p-level.
proofSteps: Take the scheme-theoretic Zariski closure in the Siegel model and then its normalization in the generic Hodge variety.
Retain the full fixer and connected parahoric as distinct data; use the induced lattice or lattice-chain Siegel level.
acceptance: A parahoric label alone must not certify the tensor-compatible deformation theorem.

sources.match: KZ specifies the global lattice and tensor setup; KPZ supplies the corrected distinction between good and very good embeddings.

nodes.title: Integral Shimura stacks
nodes.statement: For a possibly non-neat K^p, choose neat normal K_1^p inside it and form the quotient stack [S_(K_p K_1^p)/(K^p/K_1^p)]. Comparison through a common neat normal subgroup makes this independent up to canonical equivalence. The generic fibre is the Shimura stack, and the construction carries the compatible prime-to-p Hecke action. A coarse quotient is not substituted for this stack.
proofSteps: KZ permits arbitrary prime-to-p level by taking a quotient of a neat model.
Pull the normalized models to a common finite étale level and apply quotient-stack descent.
acceptance: Stabilizers at non-neat points remain visible.

nodes.title: Prime-to-p integral tower
nodes.statement: For a fixed admissible p-level and nested sufficiently small prime-to-p levels K_1^p normal in K_2^p, the transition S_(K_pK_1^p)→S_(K_pK_2^p) is finite étale with the expected finite level action; the pro-object carries a continuous G(A_f^p)-action. On normal components the promoted tensor-compatible level sections are uniquely determined by their generic restrictions.
proofSteps: HT constructs the prime-to-p tower and extends its tensor-compatible sections across the normal model.
Use the finite étale Siegel level maps and normalization to transfer the transition maps; extend equality of sections by normality.

nodes.title: Integral étale Hodge tensors
nodes.statement: Pull the universal abelian scheme to a neat Hodge model. Its absolute Hodge tensors give prime-to-p étale tensor sections on H¹ and, by mixed-tensor duality, on H₁=T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ. They are invariant under the arithmetic fundamental group and compatible with Hecke maps and base change. The tower torsor is Isom_tensor(V_Qℓ,H₁), rather than the frame torsor of H¹. The cohomological realization H¹=H₁∨ is its contragredient; for a symplectic representation of multiplier c, H₁∨≅H₁⊗c⁻¹. Geometric q-Frobenius has multiplier q⁻¹ on H₁ and q on H¹.
proofSteps: KZ identifies the tower frame torsor with the étale realizations of the defining Hodge tensors.
Use the generic absolute-Hodge realization and normal extension of prime-to-p sections, then descend from neat covers.
acceptance: The polarization is a similitude tensor with its Tate line; its scalar multiplier is not forced to one.

sources.match: KZ identifies the tower frame torsor with the étale realizations of the defining Hodge tensors.

nodes.title: Lift-independent crystalline tensors
nodes.statement: For a geometric special-fibre point x of the normal Hodge model, every characteristic-zero lift through x gives the same rational Frobenius-invariant tensors in D(A_x[p∞])[1/p]^⊗, under the crystalline–de Rham comparisons. This independence holds across the lifts belonging to that normalization point; equality of underlying Siegel points alone does not identify different normalization branches. Integrality is a separate assertion requiring the integral embedding input.
proofSteps: HT uses horizontal transport on the connected normal formal neighbourhood to compare the realizations from different lifts.
Apply crystalline–de Rham compatibility for absolute Hodge cycles and uniqueness of parallel sections on the rigid generic fibre.
acceptance: Do not deduce integral tensors solely from rational comparison.

sources.match: HT uses horizontal transport on the connected normal formal neighbourhood to compare the realizations from different lifts.

nodes.title: Universal crystalline tensor functor
nodes.statement: On the geometric special fibre of a neat normal Hodge model, the universal abelian p-divisible group determines a convergent F-isocrystal D together with global Frobenius-invariant defining tensors. Their fibres are the lift-independent tensors. Tensor frames give an exact faithful Q_p-linear tensor functor Rep(G_Qp)→F-Isoc(S_k), sending the dual of the standard tower representation to D, with scalar-extended fibre functors over L=Frac W(k). After scalar extension and choice of fibre functor, the Tannakian group H of the category generated by D is a subgroup of the tensor stabilizer in the cohomological representation; it need not be the full group. Geometric monodromy after forgetting Frobenius is a different subgroup.
proofSteps: HT globalizes the crystalline tensor sections using semistable alterations and proper descent.
Import the general log-Dieudonné comparison, alteration descent and convergent-isocrystal full faithfulness; specialize them to the universal Hodge family.
Construct the Rep(G)-functor through the tensor frame torsor. Restriction to H explains why generated-category equivalence with all Rep(G) is unnecessary.
acceptance: For a constant ordinary elliptic family, Frobenius-forgetting geometric monodromy is trivial, but the category generated by D contains its determinant 1(−1), so H has a nontrivial slope-torus quotient.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.3.12 and Corollary 1.3.13, p.19; Appendix A.4–A.7, pp.38–39

nodes.title: Adapted normalization branches
nodes.statement: For the good Hodge normalization with G^fix=G°, neat K^p, and x above a point of the Siegel closure, assume the embedding is very good at its corresponding local-model point y. The completion of the chosen normalization component identifies with the versal (G,μ)-adapted deformation ring R_G. An integral lift belongs to this branch exactly when its p-divisible group with the specified tensors is adapted. The condition uses the integral Frobenius tensors and the G-split Hodge filtration, not only the rational Newton class.
proofSteps: Apply the supplier versal adapted deformation theorem at y.
Use Serre–Tate and integral point recognition to identify the chosen branch, in both directions.
acceptance: The adapted-ring comparison must name a particular normalization branch.

nodes.title: Pointwise Hodge comparison
nodes.statement: For p>2 and a geometric point x of the normalized Hodge model, choose a lift over O_K, with K a finite totally ramified extension of breve Q_p, and the prescribed smooth full-fixer integral tensor stabilizer. Apply the integral tensor comparison to the abelian fibre: the canonical tensors at x are integral in its contravariant Dieudonné module, the W(k)-frame transports the chosen lattice dual and tensors to that module, and the lift filtration is induced by a G-cocharacter conjugate to μ_h inverse. This is the Shimura point specialization of the imported comparison; the general crystalline tensor theorem and torsor triviality are owned by its supplier.
proofSteps: Identify the p-adic absolute Hodge tensors of the abelian lift and apply the integral tensor supplier.
Transport the integral frame to crystalline and de Rham evaluation as in KZ §4.1.7.
acceptance: Rationally equal tensors with different integral lattices do not pass this statement.

nodes.title: Tensors distinguish normalization points
nodes.statement: Suppose two geometric points of the normal Hodge model have the same image in the Siegel closure and the induced identification of their abelian varieties identifies all their crystalline tensors. For a good Hodge normalization with G^fix=G°, neat K^p and very-goodness at the corresponding point y, the two normalization points are equal. No assertion is made from equality of the underlying abelian varieties without the tensors.
proofSteps: KZ detects the normalization branch by its adapted tensor deformation ring.
The common tensors select the same completed component; use finiteness of normalization and the branch criterion to identify the points.
acceptance: The identity on a Siegel fibre must still be tested on the complete tensor family.

sources.match: KZ detects the normalization branch by its adapted tensor deformation ring.

nodes.title: Hodge local-model diagram
nodes.statement: For the very-good full-fixer Hodge model of KPZ 7.1.2, the scheme of integral de Rham tensor frames is a G^fix-torsor π:S̃→S. Sending a frame to the Hodge filtration gives an equivariant smooth map q:S̃→M_loc(G,{μ_h}) of relative dimension dim G. The local model is the imported canonical flat closure. The smooth action morphism G^fix×M_loc→M_loc is not asserted to be a torsor.
hypotheses: Corrected Hodge setup (KPZ 7.1.2): p>2; G^fix is the stabilizer at a point generic in its facet; K_p=G^fix(Z_p); G_Qp is R-smooth and p does not divide |π₁(G_der,Qp)|; the Hodge embedding extends to a very-good integral embedding G^fix→GL(Λ), with Λ contained in its symplectic dual. Prime-to-p levels are sufficiently small and compatible with the Siegel embedding.
proofSteps: KPZ repairs the tensor-compatible local-model comparison and proves smoothness of the frame-to-filtration map.
Glue local tensor frames and identify the deformation map with the local-model action chart using the very-good trivialization.
acceptance: Separate the torsor map π from the smooth map q.

sources.match: KPZ repairs the tensor-compatible local-model comparison and proves smoothness of the frame-to-filtration map.

The residue field remains k′. Strict henselizations alone do not supply this assertion.
hypotheses: Corrected Hodge setup (KPZ 7.1.2): p>2; G^fix is the stabilizer at a point generic in its facet; K_p=G^fix(Z_p); G_Qp is R-smooth and p does not divide |π₁(G_der,Qp)|; the Hodge embedding extends to a very-good integral embedding G^fix→GL(Λ), with Λ contained in its symplectic dual. Prime-to-p levels are sufficiently small and compatible with the Siegel embedding.
proofSteps: KPZ gives the henselized comparison with a local-model point over the same residue field when the frame group is connected.
Use smoothness and the connected-frame lifting argument in the corrected diagram.

nodes.title: Strict comparison with lattice-chain level
nodes.statement: Assume p>2 and a Hodge embedding into a Siegel datum with a self-dual periodic lattice chain L such that G^fix(breve Z_p)=G(breve Q_p)∩GSp(L)(breve Z_p). Take K_p=G^fix(Z_p) and the normalized Hodge closure in that chain-level Siegel model. At every geometric special point x there is a geometric local-model point y for which the strict henselizations, and their completions, are isomorphic. This model is canonical in the sense of KPZ Remark 7.1.9(b) and independent of the embedding and lattice within this scope. No global very-good embedding or R-smoothness hypothesis is imposed on the given datum; the modern shtuka comparison imports the corrected very-good auxiliary theory in its proof. The result does not yield a rational local-model point over a prescribed finite residue field.
proofSteps: KPZ derives the strict-henselian comparison through canonical integral-model and shtuka methods.

Use the integral-local-Shimura completion contract cited through KPZ Theorem 7.1.8 and Remark 7.1.9(b). The older embedding-independence proof corrected in §7.3.2 cannot be used without its very-good restriction. Keep strict and ordinary henselizations distinct.
acceptance: The source gate for canonical-model uniqueness remains an explicit supplier request.

nodes.title: Canonical Hodge model and uniqueness
nodes.statement: Under the lattice-chain fixer equality and p>2 hypotheses of the strict local comparison, equip the normal Hodge tower with its integral G-shtuka and its local completion identifications. It is the canonical integral model in the sense used in KPZ Remark 7.1.9(b); two choices of Hodge embedding and lattice satisfying those hypotheses have a unique isomorphism extending the generic identity, compatible with prime-to-p levels. The local integral moduli and their universal-shtuka comparisons are supplier inputs.
proofSteps: Construct the global integral shtuka from the abelian realization and glue the supplier local completion comparisons.
Use the canonical extension characterization to prove uniqueness and compatibility with changes of embedding.

api.statement: For each geometric point x, identify the v-sheaf completion of the local integral Shimura variety at its marked point with the diamond of the completed local ring at x, carrying the universal shtuka to the model shtuka.
The unique comparison between two choices is the identity on the generic Shimura tower and commutes with level changes.
Comparison isomorphisms compose transitively for three lattice and embedding choices.

tests.statement: For identical embeddings and lattices the generic comparison is identity and the unique integral extension is identity.
At a hyperspecial modular curve point both models have a one-dimensional smooth deformation ring, and the comparison respects its abelian p-divisible group.

The generic fibres of A¹_Zp and its blowup along (p,t) are both A¹_Qp, but the latter special fibre has two components and the former has one; a generic isomorphism alone does not imply an integral comparison. The canonical shtuka and completion conditions exclude this replacement.

nodes.title: Pro-level DVR extension
nodes.statement: For the normalized Hodge tower at fixed p-level and every discrete valuation O_E-algebra R of mixed characteristic (0,p), restriction gives a bijection lim_(K^p) S_(K_pK^p)(R)→Sh_(K_p)(R[1/p]). The proof uses the complete prime-to-p level system to force good reduction and then the normalization criterion. It does not assert that every finite-level generic point has good reduction.
proofSteps: KPZ proves the extension property for the full prime-to-p tower.
Apply the Siegel pro-level good-reduction criterion and lift to the normalization using its generic-fibre identification.
acceptance: A finite-level abelian variety with bad reduction is not a counterexample to the pro-level statement.

nodes.title: Special fibre and very-special geometry
nodes.statement: With the corrected local-model hypotheses, reducedness and normality of geometric irreducible components of the local-model special fibre transfer to the Hodge model. At very special parahoric level the relevant local-model special fibre is geometrically integral, and the Shimura special fibre is locally integral. This does not assert local integrality at an arbitrary parahoric crossing.
hypotheses: Corrected Hodge setup (KPZ 7.1.2): p>2; G^fix is the stabilizer at a point generic in its facet; K_p=G^fix(Z_p); G_Qp is R-smooth and p does not divide |π₁(G_der,Qp)|; the Hodge embedding extends to a very-good integral embedding G^fix→GL(Λ), with Λ contained in its symplectic dual. Prime-to-p levels are sufficiently small and compatible with the Siegel embedding.
proofSteps: KZ uses the unique extremal Schubert component at very special level to obtain local integrality.
Transfer reducedness, component normality and the very-special integral case through the smooth torsor diagram.
acceptance: An Iwahori special-fibre crossing must not be declared locally integral.

sources.match: KZ uses the unique extremal Schubert component at very special level to obtain local integrality.

nodes.title: Strongly acceptable Shimura triples
nodes.statement: A strongly acceptable triple is (G,X,G°) with (G,X) of Hodge type, G_der,Qp a product of restrictions of scalars of split reductive groups over finite extensions of Q_p, and Z_G^c generated by the maximal compact real central subtorus and Z_(G_der), such that Z_G^c,Qp is a product of induced tori. Its level model is the connected parahoric at a very-special building point: after base change to the completed maximal unramified field it is a special parahoric. The group-level adjective alone does not specify a parahoric.
proofSteps: KZ isolates these local derived and central conditions for integral functoriality and the ordinary-lifting argument.
Package the conditions with the datum and the chosen connected parahoric, exposing each hypothesis separately.
acceptance: A strongly acceptable datum at an Iwahori does not define a strongly acceptable triple.

sources.match: KZ isolates these local derived and central conditions for integral functoriality and the ordinary-lifting argument.

Consequently a chosen local reflex field for the target is unchanged on passing to the composite cover field.

nodes.title: Rational lifting to the local-model diagram
nodes.statement: For x∈S(F_q), a fibre of the connected adjoint tensor-frame torsor has an F_q-point by Lang’s theorem for its smooth connected special-fibre group. Its image is a local-model point over the same F_q in the corresponding KR stratum. The statement uses the actual connected reduction of the diagram; it does not follow from a disconnected full-fixer torsor or from strict-henselian comparison.
proofSteps: KZ trivializes the connected adjoint frame torsor over the finite field before constructing the comparison curve.
Apply Lang to the fibre, then the equivariant local-model map.

nodes.title: Curves over the original residue field
nodes.statement: For x∈S_(K,λ)(F_q) with λ below the top KR index, construct a smooth geometrically connected curve C/F_q, a rational point c∈C(F_q), and a map f:C→S with f(c)=x such that a dense open of C maps into a strictly higher KR stratum. Use the same-field local-model root-curve theorem, pull it through a smooth stack presentation retaining the rational point, and apply finite-field Bertini with prescribed point and prescribed nonempty open intersection. For a point already in the top stratum, use a curve meeting the dense ordinary open inside its smooth component. Throughout the residue field stays F_q.
proofSteps: KZ first supplies local-model curves through rational points with a dense higher-stratum intersection, then transports them to the Shimura stack.
Import the full same-field root-curve contract, including the ramified rank-one cases and the Lang argument for orbit representatives.
Use the rational-point smooth stack presentation and Poonen’s finite-field Bertini with the required local condition and open intersection; shrink to a smooth geometrically connected curve.
acceptance: The q-Frobenius at c is the same q-Frobenius as at x, not a power coming from field extension.

nodes.title: Intrinsic group-valued tower local systems
nodes.statement: For ℓ≠p, refine the ℓ-component of the prime-to-p Shimura tower to obtain its pro-étale K_ℓ-cover, then extend structure group to G(Q_ℓ). On the special fibre this defines a G(Q_ℓ)-local system L_ℓ. At neat level it agrees with the tensor-frame torsor of the abelian H₁=T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ realization; it descends as a local system on the non-neat Shimura stack. A path or frame changes the associated fundamental-group homomorphism only by G(Q_ℓ)-conjugation.
proofSteps: KZ defines the group-valued local system intrinsically from the integral tower and identifies its tensor-frame realization.
Extend structure group from the compact-level cover and descend along a neat normal quotient.
acceptance: The local system is defined before choosing an auxiliary Hodge embedding.

nodes.title: Frobenius point in the conjugacy quotient
nodes.statement: For an F_q-point y on the special-fibre Shimura stack, define γ_(y,ℓ)=χ_G(ρ_ℓ(Frob_q,geom))∈Conj(G)(Q_ℓ), where the conjugacy quotient χ_G is imported from RG3.0. The point is independent of paths, frames and the chosen neat cover. For every algebraic representation its characteristic polynomial is that of geometric Frobenius on the associated local-system fibre. A Q-rational quotient point is not by definition represented by an element of G(Q).
proofSteps: KZ sends the Frobenius of the intrinsic group-valued local system to the conjugacy quotient.
Apply the imported quotient universal property and tensor-frame comparison to remove the choices.

nodes.title: Unit eigenvalues in every representation
nodes.statement: For every finite-dimensional algebraic representation θ of G over an algebraic coefficient field of characteristic zero and every special-fibre F_q-point, all Frobenius eigenvalues of θ are units at every finite place away from p. The faithful abelian H₁ realization has reciprocals of the H¹ Weil eigenvalues and these are such units; θ occurs as a subquotient of sums of tensor products of H₁ and H₁∨, so the unit property persists. No finite-order determinant hypothesis is imposed on θ itself.
proofSteps: KZ propagates the prime-to-p unit property from the faithful abelian realization to all algebraic representations.
Use the abelian Weil polynomial and its integral roots, duality, tensor products and the tensor-generator theorem for algebraic representations.
acceptance: A determinant with nonzero Weil weight must be handled by coefficient twisting in the companion theorem, not falsely declared finite order.

nodes.title: Representation-wise Frobenius independence
nodes.statement: Fix y/F_q, primes ℓ,ℓ′≠p, algebraic closures and embeddings of a common algebraic coefficient field into them. For every algebraic representation θ of G over a number field large enough for the two algebraic Frobenius classes, the characteristic polynomials of θ(γ_(y,ℓ)) and θ(γ_(y,ℓ′)) agree under these embeddings. On a comparison curve use companions for semisimple algebraic lisse sheaves on a smooth open curve, allowing a constant twist and finite coefficient extension, and Chebotarev on its dense open. Start with ordinary points, then the top-KR curve meeting the ordinary locus, and descend through the finite KR order. Never extend F_q in this comparison.
proofSteps: KZ uses companions and Chebotarev on same-field curves to move the ordinary Frobenius equality down the KR order.
Use the unit-eigenvalue lemma to check the open-curve companion hypotheses, allowing coefficient extension without residue-field extension.
Identify the companion with the other pulled-back local system by equality on the dense higher-stratum open, then specialize to the rational marked point.
acceptance: The companion contract must cover smooth nonproper curves and semisimplifications; the projective finite-determinant statement in GS.6 alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: A common algebraic conjugacy class
nodes.statement: For a strongly acceptable triple and y/F_q, all representation characters identify the semisimple Frobenius quotient points over algebraic closures with one point in Conj(G)(Q-bar). Algebraicity of each local quotient point follows from the faithful abelian characteristic polynomial and the finite map of conjugacy quotients; equality follows from all algebraic characters, not the faithful characteristic polynomial alone.
proofSteps: KZ combines representation-wise equality with invariant characters to identify the algebraic semisimple class.
Use RG3.0’s finite faithful-quotient map for algebraicity and its full character separation for equality.
acceptance: A faithful representation alone can merge distinct orthogonal conjugacy classes; all characters remove that ambiguity.

nodes.title: Rational common Frobenius class
nodes.statement: Let p>2, let (G,X,G°) be a strongly acceptable triple (including very-special level), and let y∈S_K(F_q) for a finite extension of the reflex residue field. There is a unique γ_y∈Conj(G)(Q) whose image in Conj(G)(Q_ℓ) is γ_(y,ℓ) for every ℓ≠p. Descend the common algebraic point using its rational local realizations at almost all primes and the degree-one-residue criterion of RG3.1. This theorem supplies a quotient point; a rational representative in G(Q) requires additional group hypotheses and belongs to the downstream KZ §6 arithmetic application.
proofSteps: KZ descends the common algebraic class to Q by using its realization in Q_ℓ for every ℓ≠p.
Apply the imported degree-one residue-field descent theorem to the field of definition of the common quotient point; separatedness gives uniqueness.
acceptance: The exact q-Frobenius is retained throughout; uniqueness is in the conjugacy quotient, not in G(Q).
